title: A 50Gb/s Burst-Mode NRZ Receiver with 5-Tap FFE, 7-Tap DFE and 15ns Lock Time in 28nm CMOS for Symmetric 50G-PON
problem: 50G PON receivers face severe inter-symbol interference (ISI) from chromatic dispersion and limited photonic bandwidth; burst-mode operation requires rapid lock (<15ns) with high SNR tolerance. Existing designs trade fast lock for equalization depth (1-tap DFE insufficient for 50G).
motivation: 50G PON is the future standard for optical access networks, requiring efficient upstream burst-mode reception with both strong equalization (handling complex ISI) and fast acquisition (rapid channel synchronization).
method: A burst-mode receiver in 28nm CMOS integrates 5-tap FFE (3 pre, 1 post) and 7-tap DFE (4 floating post-cursors up to 16th tap) for deep ISI cancellation. Edge equalization with fast-lock circuitry achieves 15ns lock time while APD integration supports standard-defined high-gain photodiode operation.
key_novelty: Burst-mode NRZ receiver combining deep equalization (5-tap FFE + 7-tap DFE) with ultra-fast 15ns lock time via edge-based fast-lock design.
contributions: 15ns lock time enabling rapid burst-mode synchronization
5-tap FFE + 7-tap DFE handling complex ISI from chromatic dispersion
Support for APD (high-gain photodiode) per ITU-T 50G-PON standard
50Gb/s operation in 28nm CMOS with efficient receiver architecture

metrics.other: 50Gb/s data rate, 15ns lock time, high SNR tolerance

baselines: 6.8ns CDR reference with 1-tap DFE (insufficient ISI cancellation)
limitations: Not discussed; power consumption, area footprint, and temperature stability not characterized.
primary_theme: Fast-lock burst-mode optical receiver with deep equalization
